title: Client proposal
summary: Sell a six month pilot to an operations head and a procurement manager who loves spreadsheets.
goal: Agree to start a six month pilot with a start date this quarter.
scenario: You're selling a six month pilot of route planning software to a regional food distributor that plans its delivery routes in spreadsheets today.

attendees.name: Dana
likely_objections: My drivers won't adopt a new app in peak season
What happens if it plans a route that doesn't work?
Who supports us when something breaks at 5 in the morning?
attendees.knows: Owns the delivery fleet and the budget. Open to change if drivers are protected.

attendees.name: Marcus
likely_objections: Why a six month commitment and not one month?
attendees.knows: Has a competing quote that is 20 percent cheaper but has no local support.

hidden_concerns: Price against the spreadsheet and a cheaper competitor
Implementation risk for drivers and dispatchers
Who supports it day to day
How success is measured in the pilot
success: Dana agrees to a pilot with clear success criteria and a start date.
tips: Lead with their numbers: fuel, overtime and late deliveries.
Frame price as payback, not cost.
Agree how the pilot will be judged before you ask for a yes.
ask: Approve a six month pilot starting next month.
